Text 1 calls Asimov's style mediocre and his characters flat. Text 2 says it's unfair to fault him for that because his weak characterization serves his point that individuals don't matter over centuries of history. So Text 2's author would answer that the flat characters are a deliberate choice that conveys an important idea. Text 2 never compares him to historians (B) or praises his characters (C).

fix.passage:
Text 1
<u>Isaac Asimov, author of The Naked Sun and The Stars, Like Dust, is highly regarded despite his mediocre writing style. His prose is workmanlike; his characters are flat and discuss ideas rather than emotions.</u> That his work is enjoyable despite this is a testament to his prodigious imagination—even if people read his books only for the ideas, they will have plenty to consider.

Text 2
Asimov is critiqued for his style, but it is wrong to fault a writer for failing to do what he never intended to do. For example, although most of his novel Foundation consists of people discussing science and politics and we find out little about his characters' lives, Asimov wanted to convey the vast sweep of human history over centuries, and one of his points is that at such a timescale, individuals don't matter. Thus his lack of characterization is central to Asimov's thematic aims.

explanation: The text says hDNA "offers unique benefits," such as revealing where organisms originated. A benefit that is unique is one other genomic data can't provide, which is what D says. fix.passage: Shanlin Liu and colleagues relied on historical DNA (hDNA)—genomic data incidentally preserved in specimens housed in natural history collections—to investigate the evolutionary history of the rhinoceros family (Rhinocerotidae). Although this approach offers unique benefits, such as the ability to ascertain the biogeographical origins of organisms, it remains a relatively underutilized resource because hDNA is often to some extent degraded, a situation not easily remediable under current methodological paradigms and with extant DNA extraction and analysis technologies.

Net CO2 rises when less carbon is absorbed or more is released. In D, early snow melt reduces soil moisture, slowing plant growth (less CO2 taken in), and raises heterotrophic respiration (more CO2 released), so both effects push net CO2 up. B would increase absorption with no extra release, lowering net CO2, and A suppresses respiration, so its effect is unclear at best.

The subject is "President Mikhail Gorbachev's reforms," and the phrase between the commas is an interruption. The sentence still needs a main verb, and "contributed" provides it. "Contributing," "having contributed," and "which contributed" can't serve as main verbs, so they would leave the sentence incomplete.

A period between them is correct. B, C, and D would attach the "allowing" phrase to krotite, wrongly saying krotite lets only some light through.

The main verb of the sentence is "is" ("La Pittura... is a highly regarded example"), so the words between the commas must be a modifier, not a second verb. "Functioning" creates the descriptive phrase "symbolically functioning to portray the power of female artists." The other choices are finite verbs that would give the sentence two main verbs with no conjunction.

The part after the blank is a complete clause that explains how cells with the same DNA develop different functions. A colon correctly introduces that explanation. A comma alone (A) creates a comma splice, no punctuation (B) creates a run-on, and "and," (C) doesn't correctly join the clauses.

"That the geographic center... was conceded by all involved" and "establishing its precise coordinates proved more divisive" are both independent clauses. A semicolon correctly joins two related independent clauses. A comma alone (D) is a comma splice, no punctuation (A) is a run-on, and a colon (B) wrongly suggests the second clause explains the first rather than contrasting with it.

"Indeed" introduces a statement that confirms and strengthens what came before. "Nevertheless" and "In reality" would signal a contrast, and "Later" is wrong because both refer to 2015-2020.

Naming the course that way was a way of acting on his belief, so "To that end" fits. "In sum" and "That is" would mean the second sentence restates the first, which it doesn't.
